text:
elena: heads-up — started getting multiple customer escalations about p95/p99 spikes on hosted inference, around 11:07 UTC. Notable for models served from dedicated GPU pool `gpu-pool-3` (g5xlarge).

elena: topline: overall token latency p95 ~1.2s -> ~2.8s, p99 visible tail to ~6s. Increasing error logs about fragmented memory / slow allocator pauses.

sam: ack. any OOMs? which pods/hosts?

elena: yes, some soft OOMs observed, the runtime emitted `GPU_OOM_WARNING` and then long GC-like stalls. I grabbed the metrics:

maria: can you paste the metrics dumps? KV cache sizes, per-worker mem, and nvidia-smi?

elena: pasted below.

elena: ```
# top summary from 11:08:12
gpu-pool-3 -> host-12: nvidia-smi: 1 process using 15360 MiB / 16384 MiB
Memory fragmentation estimated: high (several 1MB holes)
Runtime logs: 2026-03-15T11:07:55Z WARN runtime::allocator: slow alloc (ms=2100)
2026-03-15T11:07:56Z ERROR runtime::kv_cache: kv_cache growth exceeded soft_limit=14GB -> current=18.2GB
2026-03-15T11:07:57Z WARN runtime::model: compacting kv cache triggered compaction=partial
2026-03-15T11:07:58Z ERROR runtime::inference: request stalled waiting for allocator (duration=3200ms)
```

tim: KV growth to 18GB on a 16GB card — we are expecting eviction but sounds like we're thrashing between evict/alloc and fragmentation prevents placing large contiguous buffers.

sam: did anything change in the last deploy? models, max_seq_len, or batch config?

elena: small release at 10:45 — added a new 32k-token context variant for the `v2-comm` family. Not promoted widely but some customers opted in. Also increased default `kv_cache_ttl` from 60s -> 300s for that family.

maria: that matches — longer TTL + bigger context -> KV per-request growth; on smaller GPUs it can overflow and force the allocator to do expensive compactions.

ashley: support got 6 reports, all from customers on gpu-pool-3, mostly long-context chat workloads. They sent repro: enabling 32k context + streaming with repeated calls.

sam: immediate mitigation: can we toggle routing so 32k-context calls go to a dedicated larger instance type or fall back to a 16k variant?

maria: yes — we have a routing policy flag. I can patch the policy to route `model:v2-comm-32k` to cpu-large or to `gpu-pool-5` (48GB A100). But need to avoid config churn.

elena: customers need a quick fix — can we set a transient per-tenant cap on max_context or force 16k fallback?

maria: two actions I propose now: (1) update route for v2-comm-32k -> gpu-pool-5, (2) temporarily reduce `kv_cache_ttl` back to 60s for the 32k variant and restart workers with allocator debug flags. I'll roll #1 now.

maria: @deploy-bot rolling route update to route:v2-comm-32k -> gpu-pool-5 (canary 10%)

deploy-bot: started canary roll (10% traffic) for route:v2-comm-32k -> gpu-pool-5.

maria: canary looks healthy for 5m, increasing to 50%.

monitor-bot: ALERT: p99 latency for gpu-pool-3 reduced by 30% within 12 minutes of canary rollout.

elena: nice. for full mitigation we should still address fragmentation/allocator. Tim any quick allocator knobs?

tim: yes — two levers:
1) jemalloc tuning: enable background threads + decay tuning to reduce small-fragment retention; flags we've used: `MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:10000,muzzy_decay_ms:10000`
2) runtime-level KV cap: set `kv_cache_soft_limit = 12GB` and enable aggressive eviction (evict oldest on exceed) to avoid growth beyond available physical memory.

maria: we can hotpatch the runtime config (no binary change). I'll set soft_limit=12GB and `eviction_policy=aggressive`. Will also revert kv_cache_ttl to 60s.

maria: patch applied to gpu-pool-3 workers. restarting workers one-by-one to pick up malloc env. Expect short reconnects.

elena: any repro steps so support can validate?

ashley: support will run this script simulating long chat:
```bash
# repro: simulate repeated streaming calls with 32k context
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"v2-comm-32k","input":"<~20k tokens>"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq -r .latency_ms
done | sort -n | awk 'NR==int(NR*0.95){print $0}'
```

tim: additional monitoring I enabled: per-host `gpu_free_contiguous_bytes` gauge and `kv_cache_contiguous_frag_pct`. If we see contig bytes < ~64MB frequently, compaction will still hurt.

sam: timeline:
- 11:07 root reports
- 11:20 route canary -> gpu-pool-5
- 11:32 canary increased -> 50%
- 11:40 patch kv soft_limit + eviction + malloc flags rolled
- 11:54 p95/p99 baseline restored to normal for gpu-pool-3

maria: long-term follow-ups:
- implement per-model kilobyte-bounded KV allocation (hard per-request cap)
- add allocator-aware placement: avoid placing large KV-hungry models onto small cards
- automatic fallback to larger instance types when kv_cache growth observed

elena: notes for the postmortem: customer-facing impact (6 escalations, 3 temporary degraded sessions), root cause: combination of 32k-context variant + increased kv_cache_ttl causing KV growth beyond GPU capacity + fragmentation preventing allocations -> allocator stalls -> higher tail latencies.

ashley: I'll notify affected customers and offer a short credit, plus mention we rolled routing and config fixes.

sam: any unresolved tasks?

maria: I'll open follow-up tickets:
- T1: per-model kv hard cap design doc (#4567)
- T2: allocator flag rollout & test matrix (#4568)
- T3: routing policy automation for context-size to instance-size mapping (#4569)

elena: thanks all. keeping this thread for the postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
